sectionAudio: Look at the middle letter first, then blend the complete word. Compare pet, pit and pat. A small vowel change can make a different real word.

pet

articulation.label: pet
articulation.alt: pet: /p/ → /ɛ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: pit
articulation.alt: pit: /p/ → /ɪ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: pat
articulation.alt: pat: /p/ → /æ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: cut
articulation.alt: cut: /k/ → /ʌ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
